text:
sam: Noticed a weird mismatch in the Go sampleapp when using the embeddings/rerank helper. Some queries get the wrong vector after a retry.

lee: Which SDK version and what does the raw response look like?

sam: Go helper v0.6. Outgoing batch (redacted):
```json
{"items":[{"id":"u1","text":"pricing"},{"id":"u2","text":"dedicated"},{"id":"u3","text":"onboard"}]}
```
Service responded with two partial arrays after an auth refresh: first chunk (fast shard) returned a1 and a3, second chunk (quantized shard) returned a2. The runtime merge concatenated results, so positions shifted.

anya: That matches something I saw: the quantized path returns base64 fp16 in field "embedding" and "dim" as string. The normal path returns numeric array in "vector" and dim as number.

sam: Exactly. Our helper assumed order preserved and used index mapping; then Float32Array conversion fails on base64 strings.

lee: Short-term fixes: make client normalize by id and accept both field names/types. Longer-term: platform should include id in every response entry and a consistent schema.

sdk-bot: note: platform PR #6310 changed quantized merge behavior last week. Might be related.

anya: I pushed a small Go helper patch that: 1) maps resp entries by id, 2) accepts "vector" or "embedding" (base64->fp16->float32), 3) validates dim equals expected and errors if missing. Test added that shuffles response order and asserts id-preserved mapping.

qa-bot: nightly/sampleapp-tests failed twice on shuffle-preserve. flaky flagged.

lee: Can we also add a conformance test across SDKs that loads two fixtures (numeric path, quantized path) and asserts all SDKs produce identical in-memory shapes?

anya: I'll add that to the SDK conformance suite. Also adding a blurb to the onboarding docs: "Do not rely on response ordering; normalize by id and coerce numeric types."

sam: Thanks. I'll update the sampleapp README and ship the helper PR. We'll follow up with platform for schema parity (PLATFORM-1428).
